newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Long OLOs shine as gold loses glitter.
newsitem.headline: Long OLOs shine as gold loses glitter.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds continued their bull run on Friday, with long bonds especially well bid as investors increasingly believed that there is no end in sight for the low-inflation environment in the U.S. and Europe.
"Long bonds and gold are both very sensitive to inflation fears. Look at gold and you see why long bonds are doing so well," one dealer said.

OLO futures were up 20 bps at 121.97, with first resistance seen at the 122.50 level reached on June 15 and next resistance at the historical high of 123.83 set in February. With the U.S. market closed, volume was low, with just 170 lots traded.
"Inflation fears have become virtually inexistant," PIB brokerage trader Herve Coppens said.
Gold hit a 12-year low at $323 an ounce on fear of central bank gold sales against a generalised background of low inflation in the Western world.
Belgian traders responded by seeking out long bonds, thus flattening the 10-20 year spread to 55 bps, from 57 on Thursday and 60 six weeks ago.
The 2007 OLO's yield BE286= stood unchanged at 5.67 percent, but the 20-year March 2015 long bond yield fell to 6.22 percent from 6.26 percent Thursday.
Dealers said the mood was generally bullish. "I see no end to this rally," one said.
Their only complaint was a lack of volume, exacerbated by the closure of U.S. markets today for a holiday. Trade in futures and cash OLOs has been very slow in the past weeks.

Money market yields remained well above German levels -- three-month Belgian yields were at 3.25/31 versus 3.01/13 in Germany -- although several economists said they expected the spread to narrow. "Belgium's short-term yield premium over Germany is abnormally wide, there is no reason for this," BBL economist Kristin Vandenbergen told Reuters.
